newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks end easier but off lows.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks end easier but off lows.

text.p: Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index closed modestly easier on Wednesday, off lows but just below its important resistance level of 11,600, as profit-takers and bulls struggled to dictate the market's direction, brokers said.
"All eyes are watching the Wall Street Dow and interest rate decisions in the U.S.," said Anthony Mak, sales director at Vickers Ballas.

The Hang Seng Index closed down 27.58 points at 11,594.03 after trending as much as 95 points down during the day. Trading was fairly active with turnover at HK$6.07 billion, although down from Tuesday's HK$7.05 billion.
The pick up in turnover this week follows months of lacklustre trading. "There are definitely new funds in the market, both local and overseas," said Vickers' Mak.
"U.S. and European funds were caught horribly underweighted in this market and are now piling in," agreed Clive Weedon, director of Hong Kong sales at Asia Equity.
But profit-taking hit shares after the Hang Seng closed at a 31-month high of 11,621.61 on Tuesday, brokers said.
Investors also remained watchful of a possible U.S. interest rate hike and preferred to wait for Wall Street's lead, they added.

Technical analysts added there remained strong resistance at the 11,600 level, the Hang Seng's previous 1996 intraday high broken on Tuesday, and said further consolidation was necessary before the index could advance further.

The utility sector led the market in a major catching up exercise, followed by the commercial and industrial sector. Finance was the most severely sold, with the sub-index down 1.38 percent compared with the index's 0.24 percent decline.
Heavyweight Hong Kong Telecom put on HK$0.25 to close at HK$13.50. China Light gained HK$0.50 to HK$35.00 and was still viewed as undervalued relative to the sector, analysts said.
Red chip conglomerate CITIC Pacific remained an institutional favourite, adding HK$0.40 to HK$35.00 on moderately high turnover of HK$219.50 million.
Henderson Land and Swire Pacific both shed HK$0.75 to HK$64.50 and HK$68.75 respectively.
In the finance sector HSBC Holdings lost HK$1.50 to HK$139.00 on profit-taking after recently hitting record highs.
Hang Seng Bank, the 61-percent owned subsidiary of HSBC, slumped HK$1.75 to HK$79.70.
